phases.name: Soldier

phases.name: Warrior
phases.note: Density clock toward 100 swings in 5:00, one-hand swings if earned, vest walks, run intervals.

exercises.name: Push-up
exercises.equipment: wall, chair or couch seat, floor, vest
cues: One straight plank line: squeeze the glutes, ribs down, no sag
Hands under the shoulders, elbows about 45 degrees from the ribs
Chest to fist height from the surface every rep, then full lockout
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shoulder, elbow or wrist pain, pain above 3/10, or hips sagging on a rep you cannot fix - drop back one step for the rest of the session.

ladder.name: Wall push-up
ladder.how: Hands flat on the wall at shoulder height, feet 2-3 ft back, body in one line from ear to heel. Chest to the wall, then full lockout.

ladder.name: Incline push-up (chair or couch seat)
ladder.how: Hands on a sturdy seat edge, feet back, body straight. Chest touches the edge, full lockout.

ladder.name: Knee push-up
ladder.how: Knees down on something soft, hips fully extended so the body is one line from knee to ear. Chest to fist height, 2 s down.

ladder.name: Full push-up
ladder.how: Floor push-up on the toes, 2 s down, chest to fist height, full lockout. If the hips sag, finish the set on the knees and log only the clean reps.

ladder.name: Full push-up, high reps (vest gate)
ladder.how: Same push-up, sets of 15-20 at a steady 1 s down, 1 s up. This is the rung that earns the vest.

ladder.name: Vest push-up, 10% bodyweight
ladder.how: Full push-up wearing the vest set to 10% bodyweight, rounded down to the vest increment (first vest session never above 10 lb).

ladder.name: Decline push-up
ladder.how: Feet on the chair seat, hands on the floor, no vest. Keep the ribs down so the low back does not arch.

ladder.name: Vest decline push-up, 15% bodyweight
ladder.how: Feet on the chair seat, vest set to 15% bodyweight, capped at 30 lb.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
cues: Knees bent, feet flat; the upper arms touch the floor lightly, 1 s pause, then press
Elbows about 45 degrees from the ribs, wrists stacked over the elbows
Single-dumbbell or bell: the free hand stays flat on your own ribs, brace so the torso does not roll
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shoulder or elbow pain, wrist pain above 3/10, or the torso rolling toward the loaded side.

ladder.name: 8 lb floor press, tempo
ladder.how: Pair of 8s. 3 s down until the upper arms kiss the floor, 1 s pause, press.

single_alt.how: One 8 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 10 lb floor press, tempo
ladder.how: Pair of 10s. 3 s down, 1 s pause on the floor, press.

single_alt.how: One 10 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 12 lb floor press
ladder.how: Pair of 12s. 2 s down, 1 s pause on the floor, press.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 20 lb floor press
ladder.how: Pair of 20s. 2 s down, 1 s pause on the floor, press.

single_alt.how: One 20 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 20 lb floor press, 3 s down + dead stop
ladder.how: Same 20 lb press with a 3 s lowering and a full 1 s dead stop with the upper arms relaxed on the floor.

single_alt.how: One 20 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, 3 s down and 1 s dead stop, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 20 lb 1.5-rep floor press
ladder.how: Press up, lower halfway, press up again, then lower all the way to the dead stop = 1 rep.

single_alt.how: One 20 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, same 1.5-rep pattern, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 35 lb floor press
ladder.how: Pair of 35s. 2 s down, 1 s pause on the floor, press. Set the bells down one at a time, never drop them.

single_alt.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: 35 lb 1.5-rep floor press
ladder.how: Press up, lower halfway, press up again, then lower all the way to the dead stop = 1 rep.

single_alt.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, same 1.5-rep pattern, free hand flat on the ribs.

ladder.name: Single-arm 53 lb kettlebell floor press
ladder.how: Sit beside the bell, roll onto your back with both hands on the handle, then settle it so the bell rests on the back of the forearm with the wrist straight. Free hand flat on your own ribs (not on the floor), brace, press one arm.

exercises.name: Overhead press
exercises.equipment: dumbbells 8/10/12/20/35 (single-arm throughout), 53 lb kettlebell at the top
cues: Ribs down, glutes tight, no back arch - the press comes from the shoulder, not the spine
Finish with the biceps by the ear and the elbow locked
Half-kneeling: the down knee is on the pressing side, front foot flat
exercises.stop_if: Shoulder pinching, pain above 3/10, or you cannot lock out overhead without arching the low back - stop the set and drop back one step.

ladder.name: Half-kneeling press, 8 lb
ladder.how: Half-kneeling, one 8 lb dumbbell, down knee on the pressing side. 2 s down, pause at the shoulder, press.

ladder.name: Half-kneeling press, 10 lb
ladder.how: Same half-kneeling press with one 10 lb dumbbell, 2 s down.

ladder.name: Half-kneeling press, 12 lb
ladder.how: Same half-kneeling press with one 12 lb dumbbell, 2 s down.

ladder.name: Standing press 12 lb, 1.5 reps
ladder.how: Standing, one 12 lb dumbbell. Press to lockout, lower to the top of the head, press again, then lower to the shoulder over 3 s = 1 rep. No leg drive.

ladder.name: Standing press 12 lb, high reps
ladder.how: Standing strict press, one 12 lb dumbbell, sets of 15-20 each side. Take the last set to RIR 0 with clean reps only.

ladder.name: Standing strict press, 20 lb
ladder.how: Standing, one 20 lb dumbbell, strict - no knee dip, no lean back. 2 s down to the shoulder.

ladder.name: Standing press 20 lb + 2 s lockout hold
ladder.how: Standing strict press with a 2 s hold at full lockout on every rep, then 3 s down. Sets of 12-15 each side.

ladder.name: 35 lb eccentric press (two-hand assist up, 3 s lower)
ladder.how: Cup the 35 lb dumbbell with both hands to get it overhead, let go with the assisting hand, then lower it single-arm over 3 s to the shoulder. Two hands up, one arm down, every rep.

ladder.name: Strict press, 35 lb
ladder.how: Standing single-arm strict press with the 35 lb dumbbell. No knee dip, no lean back, 3 s down.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell press (two-hand rack, never cleaned)
ladder.how: Deadlift the bell, then use both hands to place it in the rack against the forearm. NEVER clean it. Strict press one arm, lower under control to the rack, and set it down with both hands.

exercises.name: Pike push-up
cues: Hips high, torso close to vertical, look back between the feet
The head travels to the floor just in front of the hands, not behind them
Elbows track forward and slightly out, wrists loaded through the whole palm
exercises.stop_if: Wrist or shoulder pain above 3/10, neck pressure, or dizziness on the way down - come out and use the incline step instead.

ladder.name: Incline pike push-up (hands on the chair)
ladder.how: Hands on the chair seat, feet walked in so the hips pike high. Lower the crown of the head toward the seat, press back up.

ladder.name: Floor pike push-up
ladder.how: Hands and feet on the floor, hips high in an upside-down V. Head to the floor just in front of the hands, then press.

ladder.name: Low-elevated pike push-up, tempo
ladder.how: Feet on a couch cushion laid on the floor (8-12 in), hips stacked higher over the shoulders. 3 s down, 1 s pause with the head just off the floor.

ladder.name: Feet-elevated pike push-up (chair seat)
ladder.how: Feet on the chair seat, hips stacked directly over the hands so the torso is vertical. 2 s down, head to the floor, press to lockout.

ladder.name: Deficit feet-elevated pike push-up
ladder.how: Feet on the chair seat, hands on a firm couch cushion (or two thick books) on the floor, so the head can travel below hand level. Lower until the head clears the hands, then press.

ladder.name: Chest-to-wall handstand hold
ladder.how: Hands 8-12 in from the wall, walk the feet up the wall until the chest and hips are close to it. Ribs down, squeeze the glutes, breathe. Come down the moment the line breaks. Finish the block with one easy set of feet-elevated pike push-ups (not scored).

exercises.name: Diamond push-up
exercises.equipment: wall, chair or couch seat, floor, vest
cues: Index fingers and thumbs form a diamond under the sternum
Elbows brush past the ribs, never flare wide; chest touches the hands
One straight line from ear to heel, glutes squeezed
exercises.stop_if: Pain on the inside or point of the elbow, wrist pain above 3/10, or the elbows flaring to finish a rep - move the hands 2 in apart or drop back one step.

ladder.name: Wall diamond push-up
ladder.how: Hands in a diamond on the wall at chest height, feet 2-3 ft back. Elbows stay close to the ribs.

ladder.name: Incline diamond push-up (chair)
ladder.how: Hands in a diamond on the chair seat, body straight, chest to the hands.

ladder.name: Knee diamond push-up
ladder.how: Knees down, hips fully extended, hands in a diamond under the sternum. 2 s down.

ladder.name: Full diamond push-up
ladder.how: Floor diamond push-up on the toes, chest to the hands, full lockout.

ladder.name: Vest diamond push-up, 10% bodyweight
ladder.how: Full diamond push-up wearing the vest at 10% bodyweight, rounded down to the vest increment.

exercises.name: Overhead triceps extension
cues: Both hands cup the top plate; the elbows point forward and stay narrow
Full stretch until the forearm touches the biceps, then full lockout
Ribs down and glutes tight - the low back does not arch to finish the rep
exercises.stop_if: Elbow pain, a sore point on the inside of the elbow, or the elbows flaring wide to finish - stop the set and drop back one step.

ladder.name: 8 lb overhead extension
ladder.how: One 8 lb dumbbell, both hands cupping the top plate, seated or standing tall. 3 s down to a full stretch behind the head, then lock out.

ladder.name: 10 lb overhead extension
ladder.how: One 10 lb dumbbell, both hands on the top plate, 3 s down.

ladder.name: 12 lb overhead extension
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, both hands on the top plate, 3 s down.

ladder.name: 20 lb overhead extension, 3 s eccentric
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell, both hands on the top plate. 3 s down under full control, press back to lockout.

ladder.name: 20 lb overhead extension + 1 s stretch pause
ladder.how: Same 20 lb extension, 3 s down and a full 1 s pause at the deepest stretch before pressing back up.

ladder.name: 35 lb overhead extension, high reps
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, both hands on the top plate, 2 s down. Start where you are and build the sets toward 15 clean reps.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
cues: Lead with the elbows and stop at shoulder height, no higher
Slight forward lean, no swing, no shrug - the traps stay down
3 s lower on every rep
exercises.stop_if: Pinching at the top of the shoulder, trap or neck cramping, or pain above 3/10 - cut the range to just below shoulder height or drop back one step.

ladder.name: 8 lb lateral raise
ladder.how: Pair of 8s. 2 s up to shoulder height, 3 s down, thumbs level with the little fingers.

single_alt.how: One 8 lb dumbbell, alternate sides; free hand rests on the hip.

ladder.name: 10 lb lateral raise
ladder.how: Pair of 10s, 2 s up, 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One 10 lb dumbbell, alternate sides; free hand rests on the hip.

ladder.name: 12 lb lateral raise
ladder.how: Pair of 12s, 2 s up, 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, alternate sides; free hand rests on the hip.

ladder.name: 12 lb raise, 1 s top pause
ladder.how: Pair of 12s. Hold 1 s at shoulder height with the traps down, then 3 s lower.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, alternate sides, 1 s hold at the top.

ladder.name: 12 lb 1.5-rep raise
ladder.how: Up to shoulder height, halfway down, back up, then all the way down = 1 rep.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, alternate sides, same 1.5-rep pattern.

ladder.name: 12 lb raise, 20 reps + 10 partials
ladder.how: 20 full raises, then without resting add 10 partial raises from the bottom to about halfway. Log the full reps only; the partials are part of the set.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, alternate sides: 20 full raises then 10 partials per side.

ladder.name: 20 lb lean-away single-arm raise
ladder.how: Hold the chair back with the free hand and lean away from it, then raise one 20 lb dumbbell to shoulder height, 3 s down. Optional terminal rung - stay on the 12 lb partials step if 20 lb forces a shrug or a swing.

exercises.name: Single-arm row (chair supported)
exercises.equipment: chair, dumbbells 12/20/35 (single is enough), 53 lb kettlebell
cues: Hand and same-side knee on the chair, back flat, hips square
Elbow to the hip pocket, 1 s squeeze, full stretch at the bottom
No torso rotation and no shrug: the shoulder blade slides, it does not hike
Tuesday is the light day (3 sets, leave 2-3 reps in the tank); Friday is the heavy day (4 sets, chase the top of the range)
exercises.stop_if: Sharp pain in the shoulder, elbow or low back, any pinch under the shoulder blade, or a back that rounds and will not flatten between reps

ladder.name: 12 lb row
ladder.how: Hand and knee on the chair, spine long. 2 s down, 1 s squeeze. Tuesday 3 sets at the low end; Friday 4 sets toward the high end.

ladder.name: 20 lb row
ladder.how: Same setup and tempo, heavier bell. Friday's fourth set may be 2-3 reps lower than the first three; that is fine, it is the advance rule that matters.

ladder.name: 20 lb row, 2 s top pause
ladder.how: Same 20 lb, but hold the squeeze 2 s at the top of every rep. Higher reps, same load: this is the bridge to 35 lb.

ladder.name: 35 lb row
ladder.how: Controlled, no yank and no twist. If the torso rotates to start the rep, the set is over.

ladder.name: 35 lb row, 3 s down + 1 s pause
ladder.how: 3 s lowering, 1 s squeeze at the top. Reps climb on the same 35 lb until the 53 lb bell is earned.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell row
ladder.how: Bell by the handle, hand and knee on the chair. Picking the bell up off the floor is a deadlift: hinge to it, flat back, stand it up, then set up. Friday only if Tuesday felt heavy.

ladder.name: 53 lb gorilla row
ladder.how: Wide stance, hinge held, bell on the floor between the feet. Row one side while the free hand rests on the floor or on the bell; alternate sides. Reset the hinge between reps if the back rounds.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W raises
cues: Forehead on a folded towel, neck neutral, eyes down
Lift from the shoulder blades, not the low back; 2 s hold at the top
Thumbs up in the Y and T, thumbs up and elbows bent in the W; glutes lightly on to keep the ribs down
exercises.stop_if: Low-back pinching, neck strain, or any letter you can only lift by arching

ladder.name: Bodyweight Y-T-W
ladder.how: Face down. All reps of the Y, then the T, then the W. All three letters together = one set.

ladder.name: Bodyweight Y-T-W, 2 s holds
ladder.how: Same three letters, but hold the top of every rep for a full 2 s before lowering.

ladder.name: 8 lb Y-T-W
ladder.how: 8 lb in each hand, 2 s hold. The Y is the hardest letter, so it gets the lowest target.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps of a letter with the loaded arm while the other arm does the same letter empty, then swap. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 10 lb Y-T-W
ladder.how: 10 lb in each hand, 2 s hold. Same three letters, same order.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps of a letter with the loaded arm, the other arm empty, then swap. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 12 lb Y-T-W, 2 s hold
ladder.how: 12 lb in each hand, full 2 s hold on every rep. This is the top of the ladder: hold the quality, do not chase load.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps of a letter with the loaded arm, the other arm empty, then swap. Both arms = one set.

exercises.name: Bent-over rear delt fly
cues: Hinge to 45 degrees or more, flat back, chest proud
Sweep out and back with thumbs down, 1 s squeeze, no shrug
Soft elbows held at a fixed angle: this is a fly, not a row
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shoulder pain, low-back rounding you cannot fix, or reps that only move when you jerk the torso

ladder.name: Prone T raise (bodyweight)
ladder.how: Face down on the floor, arms straight out in a T, thumbs up. Lift, hold 2 s, lower with control.

ladder.name: 8 lb fly
ladder.how: Hinged over, 3 s down on every rep.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: free hand braced on the chair seat, all reps one side, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 10 lb fly
ladder.how: Same hinge, same 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: free hand braced on the chair seat, all reps one side, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 12 lb fly, 1 s top pause
ladder.how: 3 s down, 1 s squeeze at the top. The pause is what bridges 12 lb to 20 lb.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: free hand braced on the chair seat, all reps one side, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 20 lb fly
ladder.how: 2 s down, strict. If the elbow angle opens and closes, the load is too heavy: go back to the 12 lb pause step.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: free hand braced on the chair seat, all reps one side, then swap. Both sides = one set.

exercises.name: Dumbbell biceps curl
cues: Elbows pinned to the ribs, no swing and no lean back
Full extension at the bottom, palm turns up at the top
Lower for 2 s: the way down is where the arm is built
exercises.stop_if: Elbow or forearm-tendon pain, or a rep that only moves when the hips do

ladder.name: 8 lb curl
ladder.how: Both arms together, 2 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 10 lb curl
ladder.how: Same strict form, 2 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 12 lb curl
ladder.how: Same strict form, 2 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 12 lb curl, tempo 3-1-3
ladder.how: 3 s up, 1 s squeeze, 3 s down. Same 12 lb: time under tension is the bridge to 20 lb.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 20 lb curl
ladder.how: Strict, elbows pinned, no body english.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 20 lb 1.5-rep curl
ladder.how: Curl all the way up, lower halfway, curl up again, then lower fully. That whole sequence is one rep.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 35 lb alternating curl
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, strict. Brace the free hand on the hip; no leaning back, no hip drive.

exercises.name: Hammer curl (brachialis + forearms)
cues: Thumbs up the whole way, elbows pinned, 3 s lower
Crush the handle: this is forearm and grip work too
Shoulders stay down and back; the wrist stays straight, never cocked back
exercises.stop_if: Wrist, elbow or forearm-tendon pain, or grip failing before the arm does two sets running

ladder.name: 8 lb hammer curl
ladder.how: One 8 lb dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other the whole way (thumbs up, like holding a hammer). Elbows pinned to your ribs, curl to the shoulder without swinging, then take 3 seconds to lower.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 10 lb hammer curl
ladder.how: Same neutral grip, 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 12 lb hammer curl
ladder.how: Same neutral grip, 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 20 lb hammer curl
ladder.how: Controlled, elbows pinned. Expect the grip to talk first.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 20 lb hammer curl, tempo
ladder.how: 3 s eccentric, 1 s pause at the top. Same 20 lb, more reps: the bridge to 35 lb.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps with one arm, 20 s rest, all reps with the other. Both arms = one set.

ladder.name: 35 lb cross-body hammer curl
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, one arm at a time, curling across the body toward the opposite shoulder. Free hand on the hip, torso still.

exercises.name: Dumbbell / kettlebell shrug
cues: Straight up toward the ears, 2 s hold at the top, 3 s down; never roll the shoulders
Chin tucked, arms hanging long and relaxed: the traps do all the work
One implement: hold it on one side, shrug that side, and refuse to side-bend toward it
exercises.stop_if: Neck pain, tingling into the arms or hands, headache, or a top position you can only reach by tilting the head

ladder.name: 12 lb shrug
ladder.how: One dumbbell in each hand, standing tall. 2 s hold at the top, 3 s down.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps on one side while the free hand rests on the thigh, then swap. Both sides = one set. Stand square, do not lean.

ladder.name: 20 lb shrug
ladder.how: Same tempo and same tall posture.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps on one side while the free hand rests on the thigh, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 35 lb shrug
ladder.how: Same tempo. Set the dumbbells down between sets rather than holding them through the rest.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps on one side while the free hand rests on the thigh, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 35 lb shrug, tempo
ladder.how: 2 s hold at the top, 3 s down, every rep. Same 35 lb, higher reps: the bridge to the bell.

single_alt.how: One dumbbell: all reps on one side while the free hand rests on the thigh, then swap. Both sides = one set.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell shrug, one side
ladder.how: Bell in one hand, free hand empty and resting on the thigh. Deadlift the bell off the floor to start: hinge, flat back, stand it up. All reps one side, then the other. Fight the side-bend the whole time.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell + 35 lb offset shrug
ladder.how: Bell in one hand, the 35 lb dumbbell in the other; swap sides each set. Pick both up with a hinge, not a bend. Stand dead square: the heavier side must not pull you over.

exercises.name: Neck strengthening (4-way)
exercises.equipment: bodyweight, own hand for resistance, folded towel
cues: Chin lightly tucked, spine tall, breathe through the hold
Push at 50-70% effort against your own hand; the head does not move at all
Every round is four directions: front, back, left, right, in that order
exercises.stop_if: Sharp neck pain, dizziness, visual changes, headache, or any tingling into the shoulders, arms or hands - stop the round and skip the rest of the day

ladder.name: 4-way isometric, 10 s
ladder.how: Palm on the forehead, then hands behind the head, then a palm on each side in turn. 50% effort, 10 s each, head perfectly still.

ladder.name: 4-way isometric, 20 s
ladder.how: Same four directions, 60-70% effort, 20 s each. If the last 5 s shake, hold the effort down, not the time.

ladder.name: 4-way isometric, 30 s
ladder.how: Same four directions at 70% effort, 30 s each. Breathe normally the whole hold; never hold your breath.

ladder.name: Lying 4-way holds, 15 s
ladder.how: No hands: the head's own weight is the load. Front = lie on your back, chin tucked, head lifted 2 in. Back = lie face down on a folded towel, head lifted to neutral. Left and right = lie on your side, head lifted level with the spine.

ladder.name: Lying 4-way holds, 30 s
ladder.how: Same four lying positions, 30 s each, chin tucked throughout. Top of the ladder: hold the quality, never add weight to the head.

exercises.name: Goblet squat
cues: Weight at the chest, elbows inside the knees at the bottom
Heels stay down, knees track over the toes, hips to knee height or lower
Big breath and brace before every descent, exhale on the way up
53 lb bell: deadlift the bell to the knees, then curl it to the chest with both hands - never swing it up
exercises.stop_if: Sharp knee, hip or low-back pain, heels lifting you cannot fix, or knees collapsing inward on the way up

cues: Heels stayed down the whole rep
Knees tracked over the toes, no inward collapse
Hips reached knee height or lower
Chest stayed up, no forward pitch
Stood up without rocking or bouncing

ladder.name: Chair sit-to-stand
ladder.how: Stand in front of the chair, arms forward. Sit back over 3 s until the seat just brushes you, then stand without rocking. Tick the 5-item checklist on every set.

ladder.name: Bodyweight full squat
ladder.how: No chair. Arms straight out as a counterweight, 2 s down to full depth, stand tall. Keep the chair behind you as a safety net for the first sets.

ladder.name: 12 lb goblet squat
ladder.how: Hold one 12 lb dumbbell vertically against the chest, top bell cupped in both hands. 2 s down, elbows inside the knees at the bottom.

ladder.name: 20 lb goblet squat
ladder.how: Same hold with one 20 lb dumbbell. 2 s down, stand tall between reps.

ladder.name: 20 lb goblet, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Same 20 lb hold. Hold the bottom for a silent 2 count with the chest up and the brace on, then stand.

ladder.name: 35 lb goblet squat
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell at the chest. Deadlift it to the knees first, then bring it up the body - do not curl it from the floor.

ladder.name: 35 lb goblet, 3 s pause
ladder.how: Same 35 lb hold, 3 s motionless in the bottom with the elbows inside the knees. This is the bridge to the 53 lb bell - own it before you touch the bell.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell goblet squat
ladder.how: Deadlift the bell to the knees, then curl it to the chest with both hands and hold it by the horns - never swing it up. 2 s down, elbows inside the knees. Set it down the same way you picked it up.

ladder.name: 53 lb goblet + vest 10% BW, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Vest on first, then deadlift the bell to the knees and curl it to the chest with both hands. 2 s pause in the bottom. Vest is 10% of bodyweight, capped at 30 lb.

exercises.name: Split squat to reverse lunge to Bulgarian split squat
exercises.equipment: wall, couch cushion, chair, dumbbells 12/20/35, 53 lb kettlebell
cues: Front shin close to vertical, rear knee travels straight down toward the floor
Torso tall for the quads, a small forward lean for the glutes - pick one and keep it
Rear foot laces-down on the cushion or seat, all the work in the front leg
Fingertips on the wall for balance only, never to push
exercises.stop_if: Sharp knee or front-of-hip pinching, the front heel lifting every rep, or a rear knee you cannot control on the way down

ladder.name: Wall-assisted split squat
ladder.how: Split stance, both feet on the floor, one hand on the wall. 2 s down until the rear knee is a hand's width off the floor, then drive through the front heel.

ladder.name: Reverse lunge (bodyweight)
ladder.how: From standing, step straight back and lower the rear knee to about an inch off the floor, then pull yourself back to standing with the front leg. Hand on the wall while you learn it.

ladder.name: 12 lb goblet reverse lunge
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell held vertically at the chest, both hands. Same reverse lunge, 2 s down.

ladder.name: Bulgarian split squat, low elevation (bodyweight)
ladder.how: Rear foot laces-down on a couch cushion laid on the floor (6-10 in). Front foot about two of your foot-lengths forward. 2 s down, fingertips on the wall for balance.

ladder.name: Bulgarian split squat, chair height (bodyweight)
ladder.how: Rear foot laces-down on the chair seat - but only if the seat sits at or below your knee height. If the seat is higher than your knee, stay on the couch cushion or a stack of cushions and add reps instead.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 12 lb goblet
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell at the chest, rear foot on the cushion or seat you settled on. 2 s down.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 20 lb goblet
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell at the chest. Set it on the floor between sides rather than carrying it around.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 20 lb goblet, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Same 20 lb hold, 2 s motionless at the bottom with the rear knee just off the floor.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 35 lb goblet
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell at the chest. Deadlift it to the knees, then bring it up the body before you set the split stance.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 35 lb goblet, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Same 35 lb hold with a 2 s pause at the bottom of every rep. This is the bridge to the bell - there is no 45 lb dumbbell, so the pause buys the strength instead.

ladder.name: Bulgarian + 53 lb kettlebell goblet
ladder.how: Deadlift the bell to the knees, then curl it to the chest with both hands and hold it by the horns - never swing it up. Set the split stance, 2 s down, drive through the front heel. Set the bell down before you switch sides.

exercises.name: Step-up
exercises.equipment: couch cushion, chair, 35 lb dumbbell, vest
cues: Whole foot on the surface, drive through that heel - no push-off from the bottom foot
3 s lowering to a soft touch, not a drop
Stand all the way tall at the top before you come down
Fingertips on the wall or a doorframe for balance, never for a pull
exercises.stop_if: Sharp knee pain, the surface sliding or tipping, or a lowering you can no longer control

ladder.name: Low step-up (bottom couch cushion on the floor, 8-12 in)
ladder.how: Use a bottom couch cushion laid flat on the floor (8-12 in) against a wall so it cannot slide. Whole foot on it, stand up through that heel, 3 s down. Alternate legs.

ladder.name: Chair step-up (bodyweight)
ladder.how: Full chair-seat height, chair braced against a wall. If the seat is above your knee height, stack cushions to knee height instead and use that. 3 s down.

ladder.name: Chair step-up, slow and high-rep
ladder.how: Same height, bodyweight, 1 s pause standing tall at the top and 3 s down on every rep. Completing this step is what unlocks the vest for step-ups.

ladder.name: Vest 10% BW step-up
ladder.how: Vest set to 10% of bodyweight, capped at 30 lb. Same chair height, 3 s down.

ladder.name: Vest 15% BW step-up
ladder.how: Vest set to 15% of bodyweight, capped at 30 lb. Same chair height and 3 s lowering.

ladder.name: Vest 15% BW + 35 lb suitcase step-up
ladder.how: Vest at 15% of bodyweight (cap 30 lb) plus one 35 lb dumbbell hanging in the hand opposite the stepping leg. Deadlift the dumbbell off the floor with a flat back between sides - that pickup is why this rung waits for the hinge gate. 3 s down, ribs stacked, do not let the loaded side pull you over.

exercises.name: Calf raise
cues: Full stretch at the bottom, 2 s squeeze at the very top, 3 s down - about 6 s a rep, so the sets are short on purpose
Fingertips on the wall for balance only
Push through the big toe, do not let the ankle roll to the outside
Two short sets on Monday and two more on Thursday beat one long grinder
exercises.stop_if: Sharp Achilles or arch pain, or a cramp that does not release in a few seconds

ladder.name: Two-leg calf raise
ladder.how: Both feet flat on the floor, fingertips on the wall. Rise to the top of the toes, 2 s squeeze, 3 s down to a full stretch.

ladder.name: Two-leg calf raise, 3 s squeeze / 4 s down
ladder.how: Same movement, slower: 3 s squeeze at the top, 4 s to lower, full stretch at the bottom. Roughly 8 s a rep, so 12-15 reps is a full set.

ladder.name: Single-leg calf raise
ladder.how: One foot on the floor, the other hooked behind the ankle. Fingertips on the wall for balance only. 2 s squeeze, 3 s down.

ladder.name: Single-leg calf raise + 20 lb
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell hanging in the same-side hand, other hand's fingertips on the wall. Same 2 s squeeze, 3 s down.

ladder.name: Single-leg calf raise + 35 lb
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell in the same-side hand. Deadlift it off the floor with a flat back, do not bend sideways to grab it.

ladder.name: Single-leg calf raise + 53 lb kettlebell, 2 s stretch pause
ladder.how: Bell hanging in the same-side hand, picked up with a flat-back deadlift. 2 s squeeze at the top and a 2 s pause in the stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Wall tibialis raise
cues: Back and shoulders flat on the wall, heels about 12 in out from the baseboard
Keep the knees straight-ish and pull the toes up toward the shins as far as they will go
Lower slowly, do not let the forefoot slap the floor
This is shin insurance for the incline walking and the running ramp - warm-up work, never a grinder
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shin pain rather than the expected burn, or numbness in the foot

ladder.name: Wall tibialis raise, 20 reps
ladder.how: Stand with your back on the wall and your heels about 12 in out. Keeping the heels planted, pull the toes and forefeet up toward your shins, hold a beat at the top, then lower over 2 s. Two sets in the lower-day warm-up.

ladder.name: Wall tibialis raise, 25 reps
ladder.how: Same position, same tempo, more reps. If 25 becomes easy, step the heels an inch further from the wall rather than adding load - there is nothing to load this with.

exercises.name: Hinge drill to dumbbell RDL to kettlebell deadlift (HINGE GATE)
cues: Hips BACK, shins near vertical, soft knees - this is not a squat
Flat back from neck to tailbone, hands slide down the thighs
Stand by squeezing the glutes, finish tall, ribs down
Weight stays close to the legs the whole way down and up
Breathe in at the top, brace, exhale at lockout - never hold your breath for a whole set
exercises.stop_if: Sharp or pinching low-back pain, a back you cannot keep flat, or the weight drifting away from your shins. Stop the set, do not finish the reps, and drop one step next session.

cues: Hips moved first, not the knees
Shins stayed near vertical
Back flat from neck to tailbone
Weight stayed close to the legs
Tall glute lockout, no back arch

ladder.name: Wall hinge drill
ladder.how: Stand about 6 in from a wall facing away. Push the hips straight back until they touch the wall, hands sliding to the knees, then squeeze the glutes to stand tall. 3 sets of 10, no load, never to failure.

ladder.name: 12 lb dumbbell RDL, 3 s down
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell held in both hands in front of the thighs (no pair needed). Push the hips back, lower for 3 s to mid-shin, stand tall. 3 sets of 12-15, stop 3 reps short of struggling.

ladder.name: 20 lb dumbbell RDL
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell held in both hands (no pair needed). 3 s down, hips back, stand tall. 3 sets of 10-12.

ladder.name: 35 lb dumbbell RDL
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell held in both hands, close to the legs. 3 s down to mid-shin, stand tall. 3 sets of 8-12.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell deadlift from the floor (HINGE GATE)
ladder.how: Bell on the floor between the feet, handle in line with the ankles. Hinge, take both hands on the handle, pull the slack out, stand tall, then set it back on the floor every rep. 3 sets of 5-10. This step is the HINGE GATE - clearing it opens every 53 lb rung in the program.

ladder.name: 53 lb deadlift, high reps
ladder.how: Touch-and-go: the bell kisses the floor and comes straight back up, 2 s down. 3 sets of 12-15. Reset to a dead stop the moment the back stops feeling flat.

ladder.name: 53 lb deadlift, hover pause
ladder.how: 3 s down, then hover the bell 1 in off the floor for 2 s before standing. 3 sets of 10-12. Any loss of a flat back ends the set.

ladder.name: 53 lb deadlift wearing the vest
ladder.how: Same dead-stop deadlift wearing the vest at 10% bodyweight (cap 30 lb). 3 sets of 10-15. Needs at least one completed weighted-vest walk block behind you.

exercises.name: Swing ladder: two-hand dumbbell swing to 53 lb kettlebell swing to one-hand
exercises.equipment: dumbbells 20/35 held by one end in both hands, 53 lb kettlebell
cues: Hike it back like a football snap - forearms hit the inner thighs high
Snap the hips, arms are ropes, the weight floats to chest height on its own
Standing plank at the top: glutes and abs tight, ribs down, no leaning back
Park it on the floor in front of you under control - never drop it, never lower it with a round back
Never swing to failure: stop while every rep still looks like the first one
exercises.stop_if: Sharp or pinching low-back pain, dizziness, or the weight starting to squat instead of hinge. 3 consecutive broken reps end the set - park the weight and move on.

cues: Hinge, not a squat
Flat back on every rep
Weight stayed above the knees on the backswing
Hip snap with a tall standing-plank lockout
Arms relaxed, weight floated to chest height

ladder.name: Hike-and-park, 20 lb dumbbell
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell stood on end, both hands on the top bell. Hinge, hike it back between the legs so the forearms touch high on the inner thighs, then stand and park it on the floor. No swing yet - this is the hike only. 5 sets of 5.

ladder.name: Dead-stop dumbbell swing, 20 lb
ladder.how: Hike, one swing to chest height, park it on the floor. Every single rep starts from a dead stop on the floor. 5 sets of 5.

ladder.name: Continuous two-hand dumbbell swing, 20 lb
ladder.how: Continuous sets of 10, park the weight between sets, rest 60 s. 5 sets of 10.

ladder.name: Two-hand dumbbell swing, 35 lb
ladder.how: Same continuous swing with the 35 lb dumbbell stood on end. 5 sets of 10, rest 60 s.

ladder.name: 35 lb dumbbell swing, sets of 15 (BELL GATE)
ladder.how: Continuous sets of 15 with the 35 lb dumbbell, rest 60-75 s. 5 sets of 12-15. Clearing this - with the hinge gate and a 30 s hollow hold behind you - earns the 53 lb bell.

ladder.name: Dead-stop 53 lb kettlebell swing
ladder.how: The bell at last. Hike, one swing to chest height, park it on the floor - every rep from a dead stop. 5 sets of 5, rest 60 s.

ladder.name: Continuous 53 lb two-hand swing
ladder.how: Continuous sets of 10 with the bell, park it between sets, rest 60 s. 5 sets of 10.

ladder.name: One-hand 53 lb swing
ladder.how: One hand on the handle, free hand mirroring the working arm, shoulder packed down. Alternate sides each set and always switch hands with the bell parked on the floor. 5 sets of 8-10 each side.

exercises.name: Saturday swing engine: EMOM to density clock
cues: This block is about pacing, not maximum effort - every minute should end with time left over
Same swing rules as Thursday: hinge, flat back, hip snap, arms are ropes
Goblet squats on the even minutes are the rest - move smoothly, no grinding reps
If a minute is not finished with at least 15 s to spare, stay on this rung next week
Never swing to failure: stop while every rep still looks like the first one
exercises.stop_if: Sharp or pinching low-back pain, dizziness, or reps that stop looking like the first one. 3 consecutive broken reps end the set - park the weight, sit the round out, and finish the block at the next minute.

cues: Hinge, not a squat
Flat back on every rep
Weight stayed above the knees on the backswing
Hip snap with a tall standing-plank lockout
Every minute finished with time to spare

ladder.name: 8-min EMOM: hinge drill / goblet squat
ladder.how: 8 rounds, one per minute on the clock. Odd minutes: 5 wall hinges, or 5 RDLs with the 12 lb dumbbell once your hinge ladder is past the wall drill. Even minutes: 8 goblet squats at your current goblet step. This is what Saturday looks like while the swing is still locked.

ladder.name: 8-min EMOM: dead-stop swings / goblet squat
ladder.how: 8 rounds, one per minute. Odd minutes: 5 dead-stop 20 lb dumbbell swings, parking the weight between every rep. Even minutes: 8 goblet squats at your current goblet step.

ladder.name: 8-min EMOM: continuous dumbbell swings / goblet squat
ladder.how: 8 rounds, one per minute. Odd minutes: 8 continuous swings with the dumbbell your swing ladder is on (20 lb, or 35 lb once you have earned it). Even minutes: 8 goblet squats at your current goblet step.

ladder.name: 8-min EMOM: 10 bell swings a minute
ladder.how: 8 rounds: 10 two-hand swings with the 53 lb bell at the top of every minute, rest the remainder. 80 swings in 8 minutes. Cut the block short the moment a minute leaves you under 15 s of rest.

ladder.name: Density clock: 100 swings in 8:00
ladder.how: 10 sets of 10 two-hand bell swings against the app stopwatch, resting as needed. Log the clock in seconds - lower is better. Target 8:00 (480 s) or faster.

ladder.name: Density clock: 100 swings in 6:00
ladder.how: Same 100 swings, tighter rest. Log the clock in seconds - lower is better. Target 6:00 (360 s) or faster. Form still ends the set before the clock does.

ladder.name: Density clock: 100 swings in 5:00
ladder.how: A set of 10 every 30 s for 5 minutes. Log the clock in seconds - lower is better. Target 5:00 (300 s). Clearing this twice, with a clean low back for two weeks, earns the one-hand swing.

exercises.name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
exercises.equipment: wall or chair, single dumbbells 8/12/20/35, 53 lb kettlebell
cues: Hips stay square to the floor - the rear hip must not roll open
The rear leg reaches straight back as the chest lowers, one long line from heel to head
Weight in the hand opposite the standing leg, sliding down the shin
Soft knee on the standing leg, foot tripod planted, eyes down at one spot
Balance first: touch the wall or chair whenever you need it rather than twisting
exercises.stop_if: Low-back pain, a hip that rolls open and will not square up, or a knee that wobbles inward. Take the fingertips back to the wall or drop one step.

ladder.name: Supported bodyweight single-leg RDL
ladder.how: Fingertips of the free hand on a wall or chair back. Hinge over the standing leg, rear leg reaching back, then stand tall. 3 sets of 8-12 each side.

ladder.name: Unsupported bodyweight single-leg RDL
ladder.how: No hands. 3 s down, pause, stand tall. Touch down with the rear toe between reps if you need to. 3 sets of 8-12 each side.

ladder.name: 8 lb single-leg RDL
ladder.how: One 8 lb dumbbell in the hand opposite the standing leg. 3 s down. 3 sets of 10-12 each side.

ladder.name: 12 lb single-leg RDL
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell, opposite hand. 3 s down. 3 sets of 10-12 each side.

ladder.name: 20 lb single-leg RDL
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell, opposite hand. 3 s down. 3 sets of 10-12 each side.

ladder.name: 20 lb single-leg RDL, 3 s down + 1 s pause
ladder.how: Same 20 lb dumbbell, 3 s down and a 1 s pause at the bottom before standing. 3 sets of 12-15 each side. This rung bridges 20 lb to 35 lb with time under tension, not load.

ladder.name: 35 lb single-leg RDL
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell, opposite hand, 3 s down. 3 sets of 8-12 each side.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell single-leg RDL
ladder.how: Bell in the hand opposite the standing leg, set it down on the floor between sides. 3 sets of 6-10 each side. Needs the hinge gate.

exercises.name: Hip thrust
exercises.equipment: couch or chair edge, dumbbells 20/35, 53 lb kettlebell, towel
cues: Chin tucked, ribs down, finish with a posterior tilt - a glute squeeze, not a back arch
Shoulder blades on the edge, shins vertical at the top, feet about hip width
2 s squeeze at the top of every rep, 2 s down
Pad the weight with a folded towel and hold it with both hands
Stop 2-3 reps short of struggling - this is never a max-effort lift
exercises.stop_if: Low-back pinching instead of a glute squeeze, hip flexor cramping, or a weight you cannot control on the way down. Shorten the range or drop one step.

ladder.name: Couch hip thrust, bodyweight
ladder.how: Upper back on the couch or chair edge, feet flat, knees bent. Drive the hips to a full lockout, 2 s squeeze, 2 s down. 3 sets of 12-20.

ladder.name: Hip thrust + 20 lb
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell across the hips on a folded towel, both hands holding it. 2 s squeeze at the top. 3 sets of 12-15.

ladder.name: Hip thrust + 35 lb
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell across the hips on a folded towel. 2 s squeeze, 3 s down. 3 sets of 10-15.

ladder.name: Hip thrust + 53 lb kettlebell, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Bell on the hips over a folded towel, both hands on it. 2 s pause at lockout, 3 s down. 3 sets of 10-15. Deadlift the bell into place from the floor - never hoist it while seated. Needs the hinge gate.

ladder.name: Single-leg hip thrust + 20 lb
ladder.how: One foot planted, the other knee pulled toward the chest. 20 lb dumbbell on the working-side hip, held with both hands. 3 sets of 8-12 each side.

ladder.name: Single-leg hip thrust + 35 lb
ladder.how: Same single-leg thrust with the 35 lb dumbbell on the working-side hip. 3 sets of 8-12 each side.

exercises.name: Floor glute bridge
cues: Heels about a hand's length from the hips, toes light, push through the heels
Ribs down and chin tucked - lift with the glutes, never by arching the low back
2 s squeeze at the top, lower under control
If the hamstrings cramp, walk the feet slightly closer and squeeze the glutes harder
Never to failure: stop while the squeeze still comes from the glutes
exercises.stop_if: Low-back pinching or hamstring cramping instead of a glute squeeze. Shorten the range, move the feet, or stop the set.

ladder.name: Glute bridge
ladder.how: On the floor, feet flat and hip width. Drive the hips up to a straight line from knee to shoulder, 2 s squeeze, lower under control. 2-3 sets of 12-20.

ladder.name: Glute bridge, 2 s pause
ladder.how: Same bridge with a hard 2 s hold at the top of every rep and 3 s down. 2-3 sets of 12-20.

ladder.name: Single-leg glute bridge
ladder.how: One foot planted, the other knee pulled to the chest, hips level throughout. 2 s squeeze at the top. 2-3 sets of 8-15 each side.

exercises.name: Turkish get-up
exercises.equipment: floor space, a shoe, dumbbells 8/12/20/35, 53 lb kettlebell
cues: Eyes on the hand the whole way up; arm vertical and locked, shoulder pulled down and packed
Roll to the elbow, to the hand, bridge the hips, sweep the leg through, lunge up; reverse the exact same path
Never rush and never go to fatigue: this is a skill rehearsal, not a conditioning set
A rep is CLEAN only when all 3 checklist items are ticked
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shoulder, elbow, wrist or low-back pain, the arm bends or drifts out of vertical, or you cannot control the knee down to the floor

cues: Arm stayed vertical and locked, eyes on the hand
Knee was lowered under control, never dropped or slammed
Every segment smooth, no rushing and no rep to failure

ladder.name: Naked get-up
ladder.how: No weight. Raise a closed fist as if it held a bell and walk the full pattern: roll to elbow, to hand, bridge, sweep the leg, lunge to standing, then reverse it. Clear 6 ft of floor beside you.

ladder.name: Shoe get-up
ladder.how: Balance a shoe flat on the fist and run the same pattern. The shoe sliding off is a DROP and the rep does not count; log drops honestly.

ladder.name: 8 lb get-up
ladder.how: Dumbbell held vertical over the shoulder, wrist straight, knuckles to the ceiling. Same pattern, same speed.

ladder.name: 12 lb get-up
ladder.how: Same pattern with the 12 lb dumbbell held vertical. If the arm wavers at any point, put the bell down and repeat the step next session.

ladder.name: 20 lb get-up
ladder.how: Same pattern with the 20 lb dumbbell. Pause for a breath at standing and at the hand position on the way down.

ladder.name: 35 lb get-up
ladder.how: Same pattern with the 35 lb dumbbell. Three per side is the whole block; if rep three is worse than rep one, stop at two.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell get-up
ladder.how: Same pattern with the bell, handle diagonal across the palm, forearm vertical. Deadlift the bell to your side and roll into position with two hands; never press it up from lying. Three per side, 30 s between reps.

exercises.retired_note: Removed from the schedule at Sean's request: seven sequential segments is too much to learn mid-session. Its job is covered by overhead_carry and bird_dog. Kept here rather than deleted so a logged rung never dangles; re-add it to wed_heart to bring it back.

exercises.name: Hollow body
cues: Low back pressed flat into the floor the whole time; the moment it lifts, the set is over
Ribs pulled down toward the hips, shoulder blades just off the floor, chin tucked a fist from the chest
Breathe shallow and steady through the hold; holding your breath is not bracing
exercises.stop_if: The low back arches off the floor and you cannot re-flatten it, or you feel it in your neck or hip flexors instead of your abs

cues: Low back stayed pressed flat to the floor for the whole set

ladder.name: Dead bug
ladder.how: On your back, arms up, knees over hips. Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly, back flat, then switch. One slow rep per side.

ladder.name: Tuck hollow hold
ladder.how: Knees bent, shins parallel to the floor, arms reaching past the knees, shoulder blades lifted. Hold.

ladder.name: One-leg-extended hollow
ladder.how: Tuck position, one leg extended long and low; switch legs at the halfway mark of the hold.

ladder.name: Full hollow hold
ladder.how: Legs straight and squeezed together, heels 6 in off the floor, arms overhead by the ears, back flat. This is the hold the bell gate is measured against.

ladder.name: Full hollow hold, long
ladder.how: Same shape, longer clock. If the back lifts before the buzzer, bend the knees slightly and finish the time in the tuck.

ladder.name: Hollow rocks
ladder.how: Hold the full hollow shape and rock from shoulders to hips using the whole rigid body. If the shape breaks, the set ends.

ladder.name: Hollow hold + 8 lb overhead
ladder.how: Full hollow with one 8 lb dumbbell held in both hands, arms locked overhead by the ears. Set the bell down on the floor behind your head to finish, never drop it.

exercises.name: Plank + side plank
cues: Elbows directly under the shoulders, glutes squeezed, pelvis tucked so the low back is flat
Side plank: hips stacked and driven high, bottom shoulder pushed away from the ear
One set is three holds - front plank, left side, right side - with 20 s between them
exercises.stop_if: Low back pinching, the hips sag and will not lift, or shoulder pain on the bottom arm

ladder.name: Knee plank + knee side plank
ladder.how: Front plank from the knees, then side plank from the knees with the bottom knee bent 90 degrees. Elbow under the shoulder in all three holds.

ladder.name: Full plank + knee side plank
ladder.how: Front plank on the toes; side planks still from the knees.

ladder.name: Plank + full side plank
ladder.how: Front plank on the toes; side planks on the feet, legs stacked or scissored front-to-back for balance.

ladder.name: Plank 60 s + side plank 45 s
ladder.how: Same three holds, longer clock. Clearing this step is what unlocks the vest for planks.

ladder.name: Long plank + top-leg-raised side plank
ladder.how: Front plank held long; side planks with the top leg lifted a few inches and held there. Bodyweight only.

parts.name: Left side plank, top leg raised
Right side plank, top leg raised

ladder.name: Vested plank + vested side plank
ladder.how: Weighted vest on for all three holds, starting at 10% bodyweight (first vest session min(10% BW, 10 lb)). Sit the vest down before rolling to the side planks if it drags the hips out of line.

exercises.name: Lying leg raise
cues: Low back stays flat and glued down; bend the knees the moment it lifts
Three seconds lowering, then hover a hand's width above the floor before the next rep
Exhale on the way up, no swinging or bouncing off the floor
exercises.stop_if: The low back arches off the floor, or you feel it low in the back rather than in the abs

ladder.name: Reverse crunch
ladder.how: On your back, knees bent over the hips, hands flat beside you. Curl the hips off the floor toward the ribs, lower slowly.

ladder.name: Tuck leg raise
ladder.how: Hands under the hips, knees bent 90 degrees. Lower the knees until the heels almost touch, 3 s down, then raise back over the hips.

ladder.name: Straight-leg raise, hands under hips
ladder.how: Legs straight and together, hands palm-down under the hips for support. Lower 3 s to a hover, raise to vertical.

ladder.name: Straight-leg raise, no support
ladder.how: Same movement with the hands at your sides, palms down, nothing under the hips. 3 s lowering, hover, no rest on the floor between reps.

ladder.name: Leg raise + 8 lb between the feet
ladder.how: Squeeze one 8 lb dumbbell between the feet (or the ankles if it slips) and raise. Have a partner or the floor set it down at the end; never let it fall on the shins.

ladder.name: Leg raise + 12 lb between the feet
ladder.how: Same with the 12 lb dumbbell. If the low back lifts even once, drop back to 8 lb for the rest of the session.

exercises.name: Suitcase carry
exercises.equipment: dumbbells 12/20/35, 53 lb kettlebell, vest, room to walk laps or space to march in place
cues: One weight, one hand, perfectly upright: refusing to lean is the whole exercise
Crush the handle, shoulders level, ribs down, short quick steps
No room to walk? March in place with a tall knee lift for the same clock
exercises.stop_if: You start leaning away from the weight and cannot straighten up, or the low back or the loaded-side shoulder hurts

ladder.name: 12 lb suitcase carry
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell at your side. Walk laps of the room, or march in place lifting the knees to hip height, for the whole clock. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 20 lb suitcase carry
ladder.how: Same, one 20 lb dumbbell. Laps or march in place.

ladder.name: 35 lb suitcase carry
ladder.how: Same, one 35 lb dumbbell. Pick it up and set it down with a hinge, not a rounded back.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell suitcase carry
ladder.how: The bell in one hand. Deadlift it off the floor with the hinge you drilled - flat back, chest tall - and set it down the same way. Laps or march in place.

ladder.name: 53 lb suitcase carry, 60 s
ladder.how: Same carry, a full minute per side. Set the bell down the moment the shoulder drops or you tip sideways.

ladder.name: 53 lb suitcase carry + vest
ladder.how: Vest at 10% bodyweight plus the bell in one hand. Laps or march in place; keep the steps short so the vest does not start swinging you.

exercises.name: Farmer carry
exercises.equipment: dumbbells 12/20/35 (single dumbbell = alternate sides), 53 lb kettlebell, vest, room to walk laps or space to march in place
cues: Stand tall, shoulders packed down and back, short quick steps, eyes forward
Grip is the point: crush the handles and do not set them down early
Only one dumbbell in the house? Carry it on one side for half the clock, then switch. No room to walk? March in place
exercises.stop_if: The shoulders round forward and will not reset, the grip fails mid-lap, or the neck or low back complains

ladder.name: 2 x 12 lb farmer carry
ladder.how: A 12 lb dumbbell in each hand. Walk laps of the room, or march in place, for the whole clock.

single_alt.how: One 12 lb dumbbell: carry it on the right for half the clock, switch to the left for the rest, staying tall on both halves.

ladder.name: 2 x 20 lb farmer carry
ladder.how: A 20 lb dumbbell in each hand, same laps or march.

single_alt.how: One 20 lb dumbbell: half the clock per side, switching without setting it down if the grip holds.

ladder.name: 2 x 35 lb farmer carry
ladder.how: A 35 lb dumbbell in each hand. Hinge to pick them up and to set them down.

single_alt.how: One 35 lb dumbbell: half the clock per side as a suitcase carry, absolutely no leaning.

ladder.name: Offset carry: 53 lb bell + 35 lb
ladder.how: The bell in one hand, the 35 lb dumbbell in the other; swap sides at the halfway mark. Deadlift the bell up and down with a flat back. Laps or march in place.

single_alt.how: No 35 lb available: carry the bell alone, half the clock per side, staying square.

ladder.name: Offset carry, long
ladder.how: Same offset carry, longer clock, still swapping sides halfway. Grip is the limiter here, not the legs.

single_alt.how: Bell only, half the clock per side.

ladder.name: Offset carry + vest
ladder.how: Vest at 10% bodyweight over the offset carry, swapping sides halfway. Cap the vest at min(20% bodyweight, 30 lb) and never add vest and time in the same week.

single_alt.how: Bell only plus the vest, half the clock per side.

exercises.name: Overhead carry
cues: Arm dead vertical, biceps beside your ear, elbow locked
Shoulder blade pulled down and back, never shrugged up to the ear
Ribs down and stomach braced so the low back does not arch
If the arm drifts forward or the elbow bends, put it down and reset the clock
exercises.stop_if: Sharp shoulder, elbow or wrist pain, the elbow bends under the weight, or you cannot keep the arm vertical

ladder.name: 8 lb overhead carry
ladder.how: One 8 lb dumbbell pressed straight overhead, arm locked, biceps by your ear. Walk laps of the room, or march in place, keeping the arm vertical for the whole clock. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 10 lb overhead carry
ladder.how: One 10 lb dumbbell locked out overhead, arm vertical, ribs down. Walk or march for the whole clock without letting the weight drift forward or the shoulder shrug up. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 12 lb overhead carry
ladder.how: One 12 lb dumbbell locked out overhead. Squeeze the shoulder blade down, brace the stomach and walk tall. If the arm drifts out of vertical, stop the clock and reset. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 20 lb overhead carry
ladder.how: One 20 lb dumbbell locked out overhead, arm vertical the whole way. Walk or march with the ribs pulled down so the low back does not arch. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 35 lb overhead carry
ladder.how: One 35 lb dumbbell locked out overhead. Press it up with both hands if you need to, then hold it vertical and walk. Switch hands between rows.

ladder.name: 53 lb kettlebell overhead carry
ladder.how: Deadlift the bell to your knees, curl it to your chest with both hands, then press it overhead with both hands and hold it locked out on one arm. Bell resting on the back of the forearm, arm vertical. Walk tall. Switch hands between rows.

exercises.name: Bird dog
cues: Hips stay square to the floor: no rocking as the leg goes back
Reach long rather than high; the arm and leg finish level with your back, not above it
Neck stays in line with your spine, eyes down at the floor
Move slowly. This is a stability exercise, not a speed one
exercises.stop_if: Low-back pain, or your hips rock so much you cannot keep them square even with a shorter reach

ladder.name: Bird dog
ladder.how: On hands and knees, hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Reach one arm straight forward and the opposite leg straight back until both are level with your back, hold for a second, then return under control. Alternate sides.

ladder.name: Bird dog, 3 s hold
ladder.how: Same movement, but hold the arm and leg out straight for 3 full seconds before returning. Keep your hips square to the floor the whole time.

ladder.name: Bird dog, 5 s hold
ladder.how: Same movement with a 5 second hold. Imagine balancing a glass of water on your low back: if your hips rock, shorten the reach.

ladder.name: Bird dog + 8 lb
ladder.how: Bird dog holding an 8 lb dumbbell in the reaching hand, 3 second hold. Only add the weight once your hips stay completely still without it.

ladder.name: Bird dog + 10 lb
ladder.how: Bird dog holding a 10 lb dumbbell in the reaching hand, 3 second hold.

exercises.name: Zone-2 incline walk
cues: Talk test rules everything: full sentences, cannot sing. If you cannot finish a sentence, drop the incline 1% before you drop the speed.
No handrails. Hands free and swinging; holding on removes most of the work and wrecks your posture.
Incline first, then speed, then duration - change ONE of the three at a time.
Land midfoot and stand tall; do not lean into the console.
exercises.stop_if: Chest pain, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, calf cramp or shin/knee pain above 3/10 - stop the belt, walk it off, and log a pain flag. Chest pain or dizziness means the session ends and you get medically cleared before the next one.

ladder.name: 3.0 mph, 0%, 20 min
ladder.how: Flat, easy, unhurried walk at 3.0 mph for 20 minutes. This rung exists so someone who cannot yet walk 20 minutes comfortably has a real place to start - finish it feeling like you could have done 5 more minutes. Hands off the rails. If 3.0 mph is too quick, walk at 2.7-2.8 mph and still call it done. If a step ever asks for more incline than your treadmill has, the app substitutes your treadmill's max incline and adds 0.3 mph; if it asks for more speed than your treadmill has, it holds max speed and adds 1% incline.

ladder.name: 3.0 mph, 1%, 25 min
ladder.how: 3.0 mph at 1% incline for 25 minutes. The 1% is the smallest bump most treadmills offer and it is only there to teach you that incline, not speed, is how this ladder grows. Talk test the whole way. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.0 mph, 2%, 30 min
ladder.how: 3.0 mph at 2% for 30 minutes - the first full Zone-2 block. Steady the whole way, no surges, no rails. If you drift out of the talk test, hold the speed and take the incline to 1%. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.2 mph, 4%, 30 min
ladder.how: 3.2 mph at 4% for 30 minutes. Clearing this rung twice is also what lets the interval ladder move past its first rung (together with 3 weeks on the program). Hands off the rails; shorten your stride rather than reaching as the hill steepens. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.4 mph, 6%, 33 min
ladder.how: 3.4 mph at 6% for 33 minutes. Three extra minutes and two extra percent - if both feel like a lot in the same week, keep the incline at 4% for one session and build the minutes first. Talk test still rules. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.5 mph, 8%, 33 min - VEST WALK GATE
ladder.how: 3.5 mph at 8% for 33 minutes. This is the VEST WALK GATE: two clean sessions here at talk-test pace with no knee or shin pain flag in the last 14 days unlocks the weighted-vest walk. 3.5 mph is the ceiling for every walking step in this app - past here the hill gets steeper, never the belt faster. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.5 mph, 10%, 36 min
ladder.how: 3.5 mph at 10% for 36 minutes. Drop to 3.3 mph if the talk test fails - the hill, not the belt, is the point. Do not shorten your stride into a shuffle or start pushing off the console. The app substitutes your treadmill's max incline plus 0.3 mph if a step exceeds the machine's limits.

ladder.name: 3.5 mph, 12%, 36 min
ladder.how: 3.5 mph at 12% for 36 minutes - the top of the walking ladder. From here the vest, not the treadmill, supplies the next hill. Many treadmills stop at 10 or 12%; if yours tops out lower, the app holds your max incline and adds 0.3 mph and this is still the terminal rung. Hands stay off the rails.

exercises.name: Zone-2 finisher walk
cues: This is a short easy walk bolted onto a strength day, not a test - talk-test pace only.
It never moves the Zone-2 ladder up or down; it only adds Zone-2 minutes to the week.
If the session is running long this is the first thing the time guard trims, down to 4 minutes.
exercises.stop_if: Chest pain, dizziness or any pain above 3/10 - stop the belt and finish the session with the cooldown flow instead.

ladder.name: Finisher walk (minutes from the day's plan)
ladder.how: Walk at talk-test pace for the minutes the day's plan gives you (Monday ~7, Thursday ~8, Saturday ~4, Wednesday Skirmish ~6-12; the plan's time_override_min is the real target, and the time guard may trim it to 4). Speed and incline are read from whatever rung you currently occupy on the Zone-2 incline walk ladder, so this finisher gets harder automatically as that ladder climbs - never set it yourself. This exercise has ONE rung and never advances or regresses: your Zone-2 ladder is moved only by the full Wednesday block. If the required incline exceeds your treadmill, the app substitutes your max incline and adds 0.3 mph.

exercises.name: March / step Zone-2 (no treadmill)
cues: Use this whenever your partner is on the treadmill - the Zone-2 minutes count exactly the same.
Talk-test pace: knees to hip height, arms driving, full sentences the whole time.
Step-march option: step up and down onto the bottom couch cushion (8-12 in) at a steady rhythm, leading leg swapping every minute.
Stay tall and quiet on the feet; if the cushion slides, march in place instead.
exercises.stop_if: Chest pain, dizziness, or knee/shin/ankle pain above 3/10. Swap step-marching for flat marching in place at the first hint of knee complaint.

ladder.name: Brisk march / step-march (minutes from the day's plan)
ladder.how: Brisk march in place, or step-march onto the bottom couch cushion, for the minutes the day's plan gives you - swap the lead leg every minute so both sides share the work. Pace by the talk test, not by speed: you should be breathing hard enough to notice and still able to answer a question in a full sentence. This is the machine-selectable Zone-2 substitute when the treadmill is occupied; the minutes count toward your weekly Zone-2 tally identically. ONE rung, never advances or regresses - your treadmill Zone-2 ladder is untouched by it.

exercises.name: Treadmill intervals (walk to jog to run)
cues: 2 min easy walk in and 2 min easy walk out of every interval block - they are part of the block, not optional.
Hard = RPE 8-9, a few words at a time. Easy = walking, and it is supposed to feel easy.
Slow the belt, never grab the rails, to survive an interval. A rung you had to hold on for does not count.
Straddle the belt during the easy leg only if you must step off; hit the speed change before the interval starts, not during it.
Hard minutes climb slowly on purpose: 6, 8, 8, 9, 10, 10, and each rung takes two clean sessions.
exercises.stop_if: Chest pain, dizziness, unusual breathlessness, or any shin, knee or Achilles pain - end the block, walk 2 min easy, and log a pain flag. If you answered yes to anything on the health screen, intervals stay locked until you confirm medical clearance.

ladder.name: Brisk-walk intervals 6 x (1 min / 1.5 min) - 6 hard min
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 6 rounds of 1 min brisk (4.0 mph flat, or 3.5 mph at 8% incline if 4.0 feels like a jog) followed by 1.5 min easy walk at 2.8 mph. 2 min easy walk out. Hard efforts should sit at RPE 6-7 - working, not gasping. You stay on this rung for at least the first 3 weeks of the program: the ladder only opens up once you have 3 weeks in and the Zone-2 ladder has reached 3.2 mph / 4%. If the incline exceeds your treadmill's max, the app uses your max incline and adds 0.3 mph.

ladder.name: Brisk-walk intervals 8 x (1 min / 1.5 min) - 8 hard min
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 8 rounds of 1 min brisk (4.0 mph flat, or 3.5 mph at 8%) followed by 1.5 min easy walk. 2 min easy walk out. Same intensity as the last rung, two more rounds - your hard minutes go 6 to 8 here and then hold at 8 while the effort changes from walking to jogging. Two clean sessions plus 14 days with no shin or knee pain flag is what opens the jog rung. If the incline exceeds your treadmill's max, the app uses your max incline and adds 0.3 mph.

ladder.name: Walk/jog intervals 8 x (1 min / 1 min) - 8 hard min - RUN GATE
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 8 rounds of 1 min jog at 5.0-5.5 mph, 1% incline, followed by 1 min walk at 3.0 mph. 2 min easy walk out. This is the RUN GATE - the first rung where your feet leave the ground, and the rung every other running reference in the app checks for. Same 8 hard minutes as the last rung: nothing got longer, only faster. Land under your hips, quick quiet steps, no reaching. If your treadmill tops out below 5.0 mph, hold max speed and add 1% incline.

ladder.name: Run/walk 9 x (1 min / 1 min) - 9 hard min
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 9 rounds of 1 min run at 5.5-6.0 mph, 1% incline, followed by 1 min walk. 2 min easy walk out. One extra round, nothing else - and because a rung takes two sessions, your running load is climbing at roughly half a round per week. Two clean sessions plus 14 clear days for shins and knees to move on. If your treadmill tops out below the target speed, hold max speed and add 1% incline.

ladder.name: Run/walk 10 x (1 min / 1 min) at RPE 9 - 10 hard min
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 10 rounds of 1 min hard run (5.5-6.5 mph, 1%) and 1 min walk. 2 min easy walk out. The rung is not the speed, it is the effort: this only counts when the block RPE comes in at 9 or above - genuinely hard, a couple of words at a time, and you are glad when the last round ends. Pick the belt speed that makes that true for you, and keep all 10 rounds honest rather than blowing up on round 4. If your treadmill tops out below the target speed, hold max speed and add 1% incline.

ladder.name: 5 x (2 min hard / 2 min easy) - 10 hard min
ladder.how: 2 min easy walk in. Then 5 rounds of 2 min hard running (5.5-6.5 mph, 1%) and 2 min easy walk. 2 min easy walk out. Same 10 hard minutes as the last rung, repackaged into longer efforts - this is the VO2max shape, and it is the top of the ladder. Pace round 1 so that round 5 looks like round 1. If your treadmill tops out below the target speed, hold max speed and add 1% incline.

exercises.name: Weighted-vest incline walk (ruck)
cues: Vest snug and worn high on the ribs - a vest that swings turns into a low-back problem.
Zone 2 by talk test, exactly like the unweighted walk. The vest is the new hill; nothing else changes.
Change ONE variable per week: minutes, then incline, then vest weight.
First vest session ever is the lighter of 10% bodyweight and 10 lb, no exceptions.
Stand tall. The moment you start leaning forward from the waist, take weight out of the vest.
exercises.stop_if: Never above 3.5 mph in the vest - if the plan and the belt disagree, the belt loses. Stop for low-back, hip, knee or shoulder pain above 3/10, for any numbness or tingling in the arms, or if the vest starts riding up on every step. Take the vest off before you step off the belt.

ladder.name: Vest 10% BW, 3.3 mph, 6%, 30 min
ladder.how: Vest loaded to 10% of bodyweight (cap 30 lb; your first ever vest session is the lighter of 10% BW and 10 lb). 3.3 mph at 6% for 30 minutes, talk test throughout. Expect this to feel harder than the same walk unweighted even though the numbers are smaller - that is the vest doing its job. Hands off the rails. If the incline exceeds your treadmill's max, the app uses your max incline and adds 0.3 mph, never taking you above 3.5 mph.

ladder.name: Vest 10% BW, 3.3 mph, 8%, 33 min
ladder.how: Same vest weight, steeper hill, three more minutes: 3.3 mph at 8% for 33 minutes. Only the incline and the clock changed this rung - the vest stays where it was. Talk test the whole way; if it fails, hold 3.3 mph and drop to 6% rather than shortening the walk. If the incline exceeds your treadmill's max, the app uses your max incline and adds 0.3 mph, capped at 3.5 mph.

ladder.name: Vest 15% BW, 3.3 mph, 8%, 33 min
ladder.how: The vest goes up to 15% of bodyweight (still capped at 30 lb) and everything else holds still: 3.3 mph at 8% for 33 minutes. Add the plates in the smallest increment your vest offers and check the straps before the belt starts. If your shoulders or low back complain in the first 10 minutes, go back to 10% for a week - the rung will still be here.

ladder.name: Vest 15% BW, 3.4 mph, 10%, 36 min
ladder.how: 15% bodyweight at 3.4 mph, 10% incline, 36 minutes. Two variables moved here (hill and clock), so give it a full two sessions before judging it, and split the difference at 8% for one session if the talk test breaks. 3.4 mph is deliberately below the 3.5 mph vest ceiling. If the incline exceeds your treadmill's max, the app uses your max incline and adds 0.3 mph, capped at 3.5 mph.

ladder.name: Vest 20% BW (cap 30 lb), 3.4 mph, 12%, 36 min
ladder.how: The top rung: vest at 20% of bodyweight or 30 lb, whichever is lighter, 3.4 mph at 12% for 36 minutes. This is a genuinely hard hour-adjacent piece of work at an easy heart rate - keep the talk test, keep your hands off the rails, keep the belt at or below 3.5 mph forever. If your treadmill stops short of 12%, the app holds your max incline and adds 0.3 mph up to the 3.5 mph ceiling, and this is still the terminal rung.

exercises.name: Warm-up Flow (walk, hinge rehearsal, pattern rehearsal)
cues: Walk first, then move every joint through its range, then rehearse the day's first pattern.
10 wall hinges every single day - the hinge gets grooved six times a week long before the bell ever swings.
Finish warm, never tired. If the warm-up is the hardest part of your session, it is too long.
Wall tibialis raises on lower days protect the shins as the incline walking and running ramp up.
exercises.stop_if: Any sharp pain during a rehearsal set - skip that pattern for the day and tell the app, rather than warming up harder to push through it.

ladder.name: Standard warm-up flow
ladder.how: 2-3 min easy walk at 3.0 mph (march in place if the treadmill is busy), then the variant for the day. LOWER DAYS: 10 leg swings per leg, 10 hip circles per side, 10 wall hinges, 10 glute bridges, 5 chair sit-to-stands, and 2 x 20 wall tibialis raises (heels about 12 in from the wall, back against it, lift the toes slowly). UPPER DAYS: 10 arm circles each way, 10 wall slides, 10 wall hinges, 8 push-ups one ladder step easier than your working step - and if you are on the first push-up rung, 8 wall push-ups with a closer stance instead - then 6 prone Y-T-W. Thursday adds a 15 s hollow hold for bracing; Saturday adds hike-and-park with whatever swing implement you have earned. This flow has ONE rung and never advances: it is preparation, not training, and the time guard is forbidden from cutting it.

exercises.name: Cooldown Flow (static stretch and breathing)
cues: Hold each stretch 30-45 s, no bouncing, long slow nasal exhales.
Stretch what you trained: hips and calves after squatting and walking, chest and lats after pressing.
Stretch to a 4/10 tension, never into pain - this is the part of the session that tells your nervous system the work is over.
exercises.stop_if: Sharp, pinching or nervy pain, or numbness anywhere - come out of the stretch immediately. Never stretch a joint you flagged pain on today.

ladder.name: Standard cooldown flow
ladder.how: Up to 2 min easy walk where the clock allows, then the variant for the day. LOWER DAYS: couch stretch 45 s per side, standing hamstring 45 s, wall calf stretch 30 s per side. UPPER DAYS: doorway or wall chest stretch 45 s, lat stretch over the chair 45 s per side, overhead triceps 30 s per side, neck side-bend 30 s per side. Finish every session with 1 min of slow breathing, exhale twice as long as the inhale. ONE rung, never advances. The time guard may trim this block down to 2 minutes but never to zero.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 1: One-mile time trial
benchmarks.locked_note: Locked until the PAR-Q health screen is answered and any 'yes' is cleared by a doctor. Same lock as the interval ladder.
benchmarks.protocol: First test of the boss script. 3 min easy walk warm-up at 2.8 mph, 1% incline, then 1.00 mile on the treadmill, hands off the rails, stop the clock at 1.00 mile. Log the time as minutes:seconds; the app stores seconds. One treadmill, two people: the second user runs the mile on Sunday in place of the recovery walk, then rejoins the Saturday script for the other five tests. 8 min easy walk before the next test.

variants.how: Run/walk the mile as fast as you can hold form. Never set the belt above the work speed of your current interval step (jog_8 = 5.0 mph, run_9 = 5.5, run_10 and above = 6.0); the RUN GATE speed cap applies to the test exactly as it does to a training interval.

Fastest one-mile WALK. Belt capped at 4.5 mph, no jogging, no rails, 1% incline. This is the test until the interval ladder reaches treadmill_intervals.jog_8; it is a real test with its own tier table, not a consolation prize.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 2: Two-minute push-ups
benchmarks.protocol: Second test, 8 min after the mile. Max clean reps in 2 minutes, rest only in the top plank (never on the floor), chest to fist height and full lockout on every rep. A rep with sagging hips does not count. 3 min rest before the next test.

variants.how: Full push-ups on the toes, 1 point each.
Knee push-ups, scored 0.5 each. Same 2-minute clock, same lockout standard.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 3: Max hollow hold
benchmarks.protocol: Third test, 3 min rest after the push-ups. One attempt. The clock stops the moment the low back lifts off the floor, the legs drop below 6 in, or the arms come down. 3 min rest before the next test.

variants.how: Full hollow: legs straight, arms overhead, low back pressed flat. 1 point per second.
Tuck hollow: knees over hips, shins parallel to the floor, arms at the shins, low back flat. Scored 0.5 s per second held.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 4: Five-minute swings
benchmarks.locked_note: Locked until the PAR-Q health screen is answered and any 'yes' is cleared by a doctor.
benchmarks.protocol: Fourth test, 3 min rest after the hollow hold. Two-hand swings to chest height, any rest scheme you like inside a 5-minute cap. The swing checklist is enforced: three broken reps (rounded back, squatting, arms lifting the bell) end the test and the score stands at the last clean rep. The test NEVER falls back to a deadlift; if the swing ladder has not earned a continuous swing yet, the test is locked and scores zero. 3 min rest before the next test.

variants.how: Continuous two-hand swings with the 53 lb kettlebell.
Continuous two-hand swings with the dumbbell your swing ladder is currently on (20 lb or 35 lb). Tier caps at soldier until the 53 lb bell is earned.
Locked. You are still on hike-and-park or dead-stop swings, which are not continuous swings; a max continuous-swing test is not safe yet and there is no deadlift substitute.
variants.lock_note: Earn swing.cont_20 (continuous swings, 20 lb dumbbell) to unlock this boss.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 5: Max goblet squats at your bodyweight load
benchmarks.protocol: Fifth test, 3 min rest after the swings. Max unbroken goblet squats, thighs below parallel, elbows inside the knees, no rest longer than 3 s standing at the top. The set ends at the first rest over 3 s or the first rep above parallel. The load is chosen by the app from your local profile (see load_rule) and is never picked by hand. 3 min rest before the last test.

load_rule.note: Bodyweight never leaves the phone; the owner's device resolves this rule and stores only the resulting implement id with the score.
load_rule.select: heaviest candidate whose lb <= 0.35 * bodyweight_lb AND whose step_id the goblet_squat ladder has reached
load_rule.below_target_note: If the heaviest ladder-reached implement is lighter than the heaviest implement allowed by 35% of bodyweight, test the lighter one and cap the tier at soldier.

variants.how: Goblet squats holding the implement resolved by load_rule. The 53 lb bell is deadlifted to the knees and curled to the chest with two hands, never swung up.
No loaded goblet step reached yet: max unbroken bodyweight squats to the same depth standard, arms forward as a counterweight, chair behind you as a depth target.

benchmarks.name: Boss Battle 6: Three-minute step-ups
benchmarks.protocol: Sixth and last test, 3 min rest after the goblet squats, then the cooldown flow. Alternating step-ups on the braced chair or the couch cushion at the height stored at setup (if the seat is higher than 0.28 x your height, use the 8-12 in cushion), full hip and knee extension at the top, count one rep per foot up. Hands off the wall except for balance.

variants.how: Wearing the vest at 10% bodyweight, rounded down to the vest increment.
Bodyweight step-ups, no vest. The vest is not worn until the step_up ladder reaches step_up.vest10.

notes: Target time: about 60 seconds per user. Screens first, then Q1-Q8, then the shared equipment card (asked once for the household, editable by either user).
swing ALWAYS starts at swing.hike_park_20 and whatever the answer to q8_kb. Both are ord 1, so default_step 'first' already produces this and no rule may override it.
treadmill_intervals always starts at ord 1 (treadmill_intervals.walk_6); the RUN GATE, not the quiz, opens jogging.

Bodyweight, height, age and sex live only on the owner's phone. No placement rule reads them, which is why the original 'goblet 20 lb if bodyweight >= 160 lb' and 'press 12 lb if male >= 160 lb' bumps were dropped: a beginner starting one rung lower costs two weeks, starting one rung too high costs a back.

locked.note: Health screen flagged. Zone-2 walking and all strength work continue as written; intervals, the mile time trial and the five-minute swing test stay locked until a doctor clears you. Tell the app once you are cleared.
Vest walks always start locked, whatever your cardio answer. They open when the Zone-2 ladder reaches treadmill_zone2.w33_8.
Wall slides were painful or blocked. Overhead pressing stays at the first rung until the slides are clean. See a clinician before loading overhead.
Sit-to-stands hurt. Squat, lunge and step-up patterns stay at the first rung until 10 sit-to-stands are pain-free. See a clinician if it persists a week.
Low-back flag: start every hinge at the wall drill and earn the pattern with the checklist before load.
Shoulder flag: overhead work starts at the lightest rung regardless of the 8 lb test.
Knee flag: start at the shallowest rung, add depth before load.
Wrist flag: press on an incline (less wrist extension) and use a fist or handles if the floor still hurts.
Neck flag: isometrics only at the shortest hold, light carries, no shrug load until pain-free for 7 days.
